title: Abu Mohammed hight Lazybones

full_text:
In Baghdad lived a young man named Abu Mohammed, so notorious for his indolence that the whole neighborhood called him Lazybones. From dawn until dusk, he lay curled upon a sheepskin mattress on his mother’s porch, refusing to fetch water, sweep the yard, or earn a single copper, while his poor mother spun cotton late into the night to feed him.

One day, an aged traveler from Khorasan arrived at the house, looking for a strong youth to accompany him on a trading voyage down the Persian Gulf. Seeing Abu Mohammed's broad shoulders, the traveler gave the mother five gold dinars and promised: 'Mother, give your son into my care. I shall cure his sloth or bring him back laden with silk.'

Dragged aboard the merchant vessel, Abu Mohammed at first groaned and wept, wishing only for his mattress. But as the ship sailed through perilous uncharted seas, fierce tempests broke the masts. Thrown upon a desert island, the lazy youth was forced by hunger to gather firewood, catch fish with his bare hands, and scale sheer cliffs to find fresh spring water.

In the mountains of the island, they discovered an ancient cavern guarded by an enchanted ape who held an emerald talisman. To secure the talisman, Abu Mohammed had to dive into a whirlpool and swim against the current. Remembering his mother’s tears and his wasted years, the youth gathered his courage, plunged into the churning waters, and retrieved the talisman with heroic determination.

The enchanted ape spoke: 'You have conquered not the waters, but your own slothful soul!'

Returning to Baghdad with chests of pearls, Abu Mohammed kissed his mother’s hands, built her a palace with blooming gardens, and opened a free craft school for the youth of the city. He never returned to his lazy ways, proving that labor and purpose give life its true fragrance.
moral: Overcoming sloth and embracing honest duty unlocks the true treasures of character and fortune.
